# Documentation for coding agents

Use this index to find the guidance needed for the current task. Read the relevant
workflow first, then consult detailed references as needed; you do not need to read
every document before starting.

## Choose your starting point

- **No Vividly workspace yet:** follow [Agentic bootstrap](./agentic-bootstrap.md)
  to install Vividly, provision a project, and begin the requested presentation.
- **Working in an existing project:** read its generated `.github/` instructions
  and Vividly authoring skill, even if your agent does not load them automatically.
  Prefer the project's version-matched `.vividly/reference/` documents over the
  latest public reference. If local guidance is absent or stale, run
  `vividly reference` from the project root.

The links below point to reference Markdown that can be fetched directly without
running the documentation presentation. Inside a project, use the corresponding
local documents.

## Create or revise slides

- [Authoring slides](./authoring.md) - Start here for the end-to-end workflow:
  understand the request, inspect the project, choose an implementation boundary,
  implement, and validate the result.
- [Slide model](./slides.md) - Read when working with manifests, slide instances,
  lifecycle methods, steps, context APIs, modules, data roots, or assets. Its
  [file-extension guidance](./slides.md#javascript-file-extensions) explains the
  `.js` default and when shared Node/browser modules should use `.mjs`.
- [Built-in controls](./controls.md) - Read before implementing Markdown, code,
  image, thumbnail, or annotation rendering that an existing control may provide.

## Add interactions and browser packages

- [Keyboard navigation](./keyboard.md) - Read when an interaction needs keyboard
  input, captured keys, or custom navigation; preserve presentation navigation.
- [Browser dependencies](./dependencies.md) - Read before selecting or loading a
  browser package, changing dependencies, or investigating cached resources.

## Preview, validate, and prepare to present

- [Authoring validation](./authoring.md#5-validate-the-result) - Use the applicable
  checks for direct arrival, forward and reverse navigation, lifecycle cleanup,
  layout, accessibility, and browser diagnostics.
- [Command line](./cli.md) - Consult for provisioning, the development server,
  local references, browser installation, thumbnails, rehearsal, and export.
- [Offline preparation](./dependencies.md#cache-preparation-and-offline-rehearsal) -
  Read when preparing a presentation for offline use; rehearse the intended path
  and report which slides and interactions were actually exercised.

## Publish and share

- [Publishing a presentation](./publishing.md) - Read when the user requests
  publishing; covers target configuration, GitHub Pages setup, dry runs, safety
  guarantees, custom domains, and recovery.

## Optional context for collaborating with the author

These user-facing pages explain the author experience rather than the slide APIs.
They are not prerequisites for authoring.

- [Guided tutorial](https://mikehopcroft.github.io/vividly/#/vividly/make-something/get-started/overview) -
  Follow the user's journey from installation to an interactive slide and a public
  link.
- [Inside an agent session](https://mikehopcroft.github.io/vividly/#/vividly/documentation/agent-session) -
  See an illustrative conversation about creating and refining a presentation.
- [User documentation overview](https://mikehopcroft.github.io/vividly/#/vividly/documentation/overview) -
  Find user-facing guidance for getting started, presenting, sharing, and
  troubleshooting.

The optional links open the interactive documentation site and require a browser.
